name: Dvali-Gabadadze-Porrati Braneworld
description: A wall with three dimensions of space in flat space of five dimensions, with a curvature term of its own in its action, proposed by Gia Dvali, Gregory Gabadadze, and Massimo Porrati in 2000. Gravity on the wall is four dimensional below a crossover length $r_c$ and five dimensional above it. On one of the two branches of Cédric Deffayet's cosmology of 2001 an empty wall expands at the rate $c/r_c$ with no cosmological constant, the hyperboloid of radius $r_c$ with two copies of its outside glued along it.
convention:
Off the wall $R_{\mu
u} = 0$, and on it $G_{ab} - 8\pi GT_{ab}/c^4 = (K_{ab} - h_{ab}K)/r_c$, with $h_{ab}$ the metric on the wall, $G_{ab}$ its Einstein tensor, $T_{ab}$ the stress tensor of its matter, $K_{ab}$ its extrinsic curvature with the normal pointing away from it, and $r_c$ the crossover length. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu
u} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha
u}$, $\delta$ is the Dirac delta, and we keep factors of $c$ explicit.
history: Gravity near a mass on a wall in flat space of five dimensions is four dimensional when the wall has a curvature term of its own in its action, and far from the mass it is five dimensional [dvali2000brane]. Gia Dvali, Gregory Gabadadze, and Massimo Porrati proposed this in 2000 for a wall of zero tension, with the term written into the classical action or induced on the wall by loops of the matter confined to it [dvali2000brane]. The potential between two masses on the wall falls as $1/r$ below the crossover length $r_c = M_P^2/(2M^3)$, with $M_P$ and $M$ the Planck masses of four and five dimensions, and as $1/r^2$ beyond it [dvali2000brane]. The graviton exchanged between the masses has the tensor structure of a massive graviton, whose extra scalar polarization adds to the attraction, and Dvali, Gabadadze, and Porrati suggested a repulsive vector field to cancel it [dvali2000brane]. For a Planck mass of five dimensions near a TeV they found $r_c \sim 10^{15}$ cm, the size of the solar system, and required a crossover about $10^8$ times larger to keep the correction to Newton's law below the relativistic precession of Mercury's perihelion [dvali2000brane].¶Hael Collins and Bob Holdom had put the same term into the action of a wall at the edge of anti-de Sitter space, and of a bubble wall expanding into the outside of a black hole, and written the Friedmann equation of each [collins2000orbifolds]. Yuri Shtanov derived the equations again for a wall bounding a space of constant curvature, and found that an empty wall with tuned constants can stay at rest or expand as de Sitter space, $a = a_0\cosh(c\tau/a_0)$, from one initial state [shtanov2000brane]. Cédric Deffayet made the space on both sides of the wall flat and empty, each the mirror image of the other, and derived $H^2 + kc^2/a^2 - (\epsilon c/r_c)\sqrt{H^2 + kc^2/a^2} = 8\pi G\rho/3$, with $\epsilon = +1$ where lengths along the wall grow with distance from it and $\epsilon = -1$ where they shrink [deffayet2001cosmology]. As matter thins out, the branch $\epsilon = -1$ goes over to a five dimensional regime with $H$ linear in the density, and the branch $\epsilon = +1$ to expansion at the constant rate $H = c/r_c$ [deffayet2001cosmology]. Deffayet called that expansion "a self-inflationary solution which produces a late accelerated expansion", credited Shtanov with noticing it, and found the energy of the wall as seen from the bulk negative on its branch, whatever the density of its matter [deffayet2001cosmology].¶Deffayet put the bulk in Gaussian normal coordinates, $y$ the proper distance from the wall, in which the scale factor changes linearly in $|y|$ [deffayet2001cosmology]. By a change to inertial coordinates of Minkowski space, in which the wall moves, Deffayet showed the bulk to be a slice of Minkowski space [deffayet2001cosmology]. A wall that is de Sitter space is a hyperboloid of the same radius in Minkowski space, $-c^2T^2 + X_1^2 + X_2^2 + X_3^2 + X_4^2 = r_c^2$ for the empty wall of the branch $\epsilon = +1$ [deffayet2001cosmology]. Deffayet's coordinates cover two copies of one side of it, glued along the wall, the outside on the branch $\epsilon = +1$ and the inside on the branch $\epsilon = -1$, where a wall with tension alone inflates as a domain wall does [deffayet2001cosmology, gregory2007perspective]. Ruth Gregory, Nemanja Kaloper, Robert C. Myers, and Antonio Padilla noted that keeping the outside mimics a wall of negative tension, and that the curvature term acts as one even when the tension is positive [gregory2007perspective]. Without the mirror symmetry the wall joins two asymptotically flat regions in a wormhole, and on the branch $\epsilon = +1$ they found the energy of five dimensions unbounded from below [gregory2007perspective].¶Deffayet, Dvali, and Gabadadze proposed in 2002 that the accelerating expansion of the universe is the branch $\epsilon = +1$, with $r_c$ near the present Hubble length and no cosmological constant on the wall [deffayet2002accelerated]. A flat universe with a density parameter of matter of 0.3 needs $r_c = 1.4\,c/H_0$, and they argued that, with gravity leaking into the fifth dimension, an observer on the wall has no infinite future horizon [deffayet2002accelerated]. With Arkady Vainshtein they showed that the exact solutions of the model are continuous in $1/r_c$, and argued from its cosmologies that the scalar polarization "decouples from the matter in the limit of vanishing graviton mass" [deffayet2002continuity]. Markus A. Luty, Massimo Porrati, and Riccardo Rattazzi found in 2003 that the bending of the wall interacts strongly below about 1000 km when $r_c$ is near the Hubble length, and that on the branch $\epsilon = +1$ with little vacuum energy this bending is a ghost, a mode of negative energy [luty2003strong].¶Alberto Nicolis and Rattazzi confirmed the ghost, Dmitry Gorbunov, Kazuya Koyama, and Sergei Sibiryakov computed it explicitly, and Christos Charmousis, Gregory, Kaloper, and Padilla found it for any tension, with the branch $\epsilon = -1$ free of it [nicolis2004consistency, gorbunov2006ghosts, charmousis2006specteroscopy]. Charmousis, Gregory, Kaloper, and Padilla concluded that "the self-accelerating solutions are not a reliable benchmark for cosmic acceleration driven by gravity modified in the IR" [charmousis2006specteroscopy]. Roy Maartens and Elisabetta Majerotto found flat models of the branch $\epsilon = +1$ inside the joint 2 sigma contour of supernovae, the microwave background, and baryon oscillations, with a cosmological constant fitting better [maartens2006constraints]. Wenjuan Fang, Sheng Wang, Wayne Hu, Zoltán Haiman, Lam Hui, and Morgan May found a flat universe on that branch nominally 5.3 sigma worse than one with a cosmological constant, from excess anisotropy of the microwave background at the lowest multipoles [fang2008challenges]. Xinyi Dai, Yupeng Yang, and Yicheng Wang fitted it in 2026 to the baryon oscillations of the second data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument, DESI, with the microwave background, supernovae, and cosmic chronometers, and found that it cannot fit the oscillations and the microwave background together [dai2026desi].¶On the branch $\epsilon = -1$ an empty wall with no tension is flat and at rest [gregory2007perspective]. Varun Sahni and Shtanov gave the wall a tension, and on that branch, which they called BRANE1, found the present equation of state of dark energy below $-1$, as for phantom energy [sahni2003braneworld]. Swagat S. Mishra, William L. Matthewson, Sahni, Arman Shafieloo, and Shtanov put a rolling scalar field on the branch with no tension, the "phantom brane", and fitted it in 2025 to the baryon oscillations of DESI's second release as closely as dark energy whose equation of state changes linearly in the scale factor [mishra2025desi].

related.text: One dimension down, a hyperboloid in flat space with two copies of its inside glued along it, a wall with tension alone. In five dimensions that wall is the branch $\epsilon = -1$, and the empty wall of the branch $\epsilon = +1$ keeps two copies of the outside [deffayet2001cosmology, gregory2007perspective].
The empty wall of the branch $\epsilon = +1$ is de Sitter space of radius $r_c$, expanding at the rate $c/r_c$ with no cosmological constant [deffayet2001cosmology, deffayet2002accelerated].

Flat space of five dimensions is the bulk on both sides of the wall, and on the branch $\epsilon = -1$ an empty wall with no tension is Minkowski space of four dimensions at rest [deffayet2001cosmology, gregory2007perspective].
The universe on the wall is Friedmann's, with a term $-\epsilon(c/r_c)\sqrt{H^2 + kc^2/a^2}$ added to the Friedmann equation [deffayet2001cosmology].

Gravity on Randall and Sundrum's wall is four dimensional because the warped fifth dimension has a finite volume. Here the fifth dimension is flat and infinite in volume, and gravity on the wall is four dimensional below $r_c$ because of the curvature term of the wall [dvali2000brane].

A wall with matter on it between two copies of anti-de Sitter space. Without its curvature term the wall in flat space obeys a Friedmann equation with the square of the density, which the branch $\epsilon = -1$ approaches as matter thins out [deffayet2001cosmology].

Dvali, Gabadadze, and Porrati suggested that the curvature term of the wall could come from a kink of a scalar field across it, a wall of the kind on which these early models trap matter [dvali2000brane].

coordinates.name: Deffayet, Gaussian Normal
domains: y = 0 \;\text{(the wall, where the side kept meets its mirror image)}

parameters.description: Curvature of space on the wall, $k \in \{-1, 0, +1\}$

Scale factor of the universe on the wall, a length, the value of $A$ at $y = 0$. With $H = (da/dt)/a$ and $\rho$ the density of the matter on the wall, $H^2 + kc^2/a^2 - (\epsilon c/r_c)\sqrt{H^2 + kc^2/a^2} = 8\pi G\rho/3$, with $\epsilon = +1$ where lengths along the wall grow with distance from it and $\epsilon = -1$ where they shrink
Scale factor of the 3-space at the distance $|y|$ from the wall, a length
Lapse, $N = \partial_tA/\dot{a}$, equal to $1$ on the wall

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, y, \chi, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ the proper time on the wall, having dimensions of time, $y$ the proper distance from it, a length, and $\chi$ a comoving radius, a pure number. On the branch $\epsilon = +1$ two copies of the side $y \ge 0$ are glued along the wall, and on the branch $\epsilon = -1$ two copies of the side $y \le 0$, so that $y$ stands where Deffayet writes $\epsilon|y|$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, a dot on the scale factor is $\dot{a} = da/d(ct)$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ is the derivative of $ct$.
geodesics: \ddot{t} + \dfrac{\partial_t N}{N}\dot{t}^2 + \dfrac{2\partial_y N}{N}\dot{t}\dot{y} + \dfrac{A\,\partial_t A}{N^2\left(1 - k\,\chi^2\right)}\dot{\chi}^2 + \dfrac{A\,\chi^2\,\partial_t A}{N^2}\dot{\theta}^2 + \dfrac{A\,\chi^2\,\partial_t A\,\sin^2\theta}{N^2}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0
\ddot{y} + N\,\partial_y N\,\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{A\,\partial_y A}{1 - k\,\chi^2}\dot{\chi}^2 - A\,\chi^2\,\partial_y A\,\dot{\theta}^2 - A\,\chi^2\,\partial_y A\,\sin^2\theta\,\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Global

parameters.description: Crossover length, the radius of the empty wall, which expands at the rate $c/r_c$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, y, \psi, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ the proper time of an observer at rest on the wall, having dimensions of time, $y$ the proper distance from the wall, with $\mathrm{sgn}(y)$ its sign, and $\psi$, $\theta$, and $\phi$ angles on the 3-sphere the wall is at each moment. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ is the derivative of $ct$.

coordinates.name: Planar

parameters.description: Crossover length, the radius of the empty wall, which expands at the rate $c/r_c$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x_1, x_2, x_3, y)$, with $t$ the proper time of an observer at rest on the wall, having dimensions of time, $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ lengths along the wall, and $y$ the proper distance from it, with $\mathrm{sgn}(y)$ its sign. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ is the derivative of $ct$.

coordinates.name: Inertial
domains: R = \sqrt{r_c^2 + c^2T^2} \;\text{(the wall, where this side meets its mirror image)}

parameters.description: Crossover length, the radius of the empty wall, which expands at the rate $c/r_c$

coordinates.convention: We use the inertial coordinates $(T, R, \psi, \theta, \phi)$ of one side of the wall, with $T$ having dimensions of time, $R$ the distance from the centre of the 3-sphere the wall is at each moment, and $\psi$, $\theta$, and $\phi$ angles on it. We take components in the chart $x^0 = cT$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{T}$ is the derivative of $cT$.
